# amux

> Open-source control plane for AI agents — run, monitor, and govern parallel agent sessions with a web dashboard, kanban board, notes, CRM, email, browser automation, skills, channels, scheduler, and agent-to-agent REST API orchestration. Self-healing, single-file, zero external dependencies. Currently supports Claude Code via tmux.

amux (Agent Multiplexer) is the open-source control plane for AI agent systems. It manages parallel agent sessions with self-healing, observability, cost control, and orchestration. Built-in tools include: markdown notes, CRM with interaction tracking, Mail.app email integration, shared Playwright browser automation, project-level slash-command skills, 1:1 inter-session channels with @mentions, a cron-style scheduler, and a file explorer with markdown editor. Currently supports Claude Code via tmux. MIT licensed. No cloud dependency. Single Rust binary, zero dependencies beyond python3 and tmux.

## Quick Start

Install via Homebrew (`brew install mixpeek/amux/amux`), PyPI (`pipx install amux`), zero-install trial (`uvx amux serve`), or from source (`git clone https://github.com/mixpeek/amux && cd amux && ./install.sh`).

```bash
brew install mixpeek/amux/amux
amux register myproject --dir ~/Dev/myproject --yolo
amux start myproject
amux serve  # → https://localhost:8824
```

## Key Features

### Agent infrastructure
- Unlimited parallel Claude Code sessions via tmux (isolated panes, permanent conversation IDs)
- Self-healing watchdog: auto-compacts on context overflow, restarts on corruption, replays last message
- Channels: 1:1 inter-session messaging with @mentions for real-time agent coordination
- Kanban board with atomic task claiming via SQLite CAS (no Redis, no duplicated work)
- Agent-to-agent REST API: POST /api/sessions/NAME/send, GET /api/sessions/NAME/peek, POST /api/board/ID/claim
- Conversation fork: clone session JSONL history to a new agent on a new branch
- Token tracking from JSONL with deduplication across restarts

### Dashboard & mobile
- Web dashboard PWA — installable on iOS/Android, offline queue with Background Sync
- Native iOS app on the App Store
- File explorer with syntax highlighting and markdown editor with find-in-page

### Built-in tools
- Notes: full markdown documents with rich Quill editor, accessible via API across all sessions
- CRM: contacts with company, role, email, phone, LinkedIn, interaction logs, tags, and follow-up tracking
- Email integration: send and read email through the Mail.app API
- Browser automation: shared Playwright instance with saved auth profiles, screenshots, and AI agent mode
- Skills / slash commands: project-level custom commands (e.g. /commit, /review-pr) any agent can invoke
- Scheduler: named recurring jobs with cron expressions and management UI
- iCal feed for board items with due dates (S3 export for Google/Apple Calendar)

### Architecture
- Rust workspace (4 crates: amux-server, amux-dashboard, amux-core, amux-cli) — single compiled binary, static dashboard files, no Docker, no config files required
- Auto-rebuilds on commit via a background build watcher; the running server self-adopts the new binary within seconds
- MIT License — free, open-source, self-hosted

## How amux differs from plain Claude Code

Claude Code runs one agent per terminal. amux runs dozens — with live monitoring, mobile access, self-healing, and inter-agent coordination that don't exist in Claude Code itself. amux does not modify or wrap Claude Code; it manages tmux sessions that run it headlessly.

## Guides

- [AI Agent Groups — Organize Your Agent Team into Namespaced Sub-Teams (2026)](https://amux.io/guides/ai-agent-groups/): How to organize AI coding agents into named groups using amux. Each group gets shared memory, environment variables, an isolated board view, and a live at-a-glance summary (member count, active/idle/waiting split, board doing/todo counts, schedule counts). Use cases: separate frontend, infra, gtm, and customer groups each with their own CLAUDE.md context and environment variables; switch between groups in one tap from the Groups tab; see every team at a glance without opening individual session panes. Groups are one of amux's eight core primitives — they compose with the board (group-scoped views), env vars (per-group config), memory (shared knowledge), and schedules (group-targeted automation). Includes a worked example (three-team setup), quick-start (create group, assign sessions, verify the at-a-glance card), and FAQ covering differences from tags, sessions, and worktrees.

- [The amux Mental Model — Every Surface Mapped to How You Already Work](https://amux.io/guides/amux-mental-model/): The complete conceptual map of amux through knowledge-work analogies, with a definition and UI mock for every surface. Sessions = employees (working dir = their desk, status dot = working/needs-you/idle); Peek = walking to someone's desk; Steering = a note on their desk delivered only when the current task finishes; Board = the team task tracker with atomic claiming and status gates (doing/done/verified); Scheduler = recurring duties (prompts on cron); Skills = SOPs/playbooks runnable as /commands across Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini (ships with /amux, /standup, /handoff, /adhd); Messages = searchable chat history per agent; Browser = an assistant with saved logins; Cost = payroll + budget report (dollar cost per task/session/model/day with cache-hit rate); Memory = institutional knowledge; Notes = wiki; Files = shared drive; Workspace = open-plan office; Alerts = the fire alarm. Includes comparison table of all 21 surfaces and a 10-question FAQ.

- [amux Is a Graph — Task Dependencies, Agent Edges and Fleet Topology (2026)](https://amux.io/guides/ai-agent-graph/): amux models every aspect of a parallel AI agent fleet as two interlocking graphs. Task graph: board cards are nodes; depends_on edges create a DAG (prerequisite gates enforced atomically at claim time — if dependency is not done, /claim returns 409); reviewer edges create completion gates (node cannot reach verified until named reviewer clears it); status is the node state machine (todo → doing → done → verified). Session graph: running agent sessions are nodes; POST /api/sessions/NAME/send creates directed instruction edges; GET /api/sessions/NAME/peek creates observation edges; channels create bidirectional persistent edges. Four coordination patterns covered: fan-out (independent parallel root nodes), pipeline (A→B→C sequential), diamond (parallel B+C merge at D), hub-and-spoke (orchestrator builds graph, workers traverse). Automatic prompt decomposition creates one node per task. Complete graph API reference (add node, add edge, traverse, advance state, read graph). HowTo JSON-LD (5 steps) + FAQPage JSON-LD (7 Qs) + Article + BreadcrumbList. Added July 2026.

## Features

- [Self-Healing AI Agents — amux Watchdog & Auto-Recovery (2026)](https://amux.io/features/self-healing/): How amux keeps Claude Code agents alive overnight. Four failure modes covered: context exhaustion (auto /compact), thinking-block corruption (detect + restart + replay), tool-approval stuck (YOLO mode auto-approve), silent hang (idle timeout kick). Watchdog thresholds in ~/.amux/server.env. Last-message replay ensures agents pick up where they left off after a crash. Comparison table: 5 failure scenarios, with vs without amux self-healing. FAQPage JSON-LD (5 Qs) + Article JSON-LD + BreadcrumbList. Updated July 2026.
- [AI Agent Dashboard — amux Web Dashboard & iOS App (2026)](https://amux.io/features/web-dashboard/): The amux dashboard covers sessions (live status dots, token spend, plan strip), peek panel (SSE-streamed terminal output, subagent switcher ▲/▼, load earlier output scrollback, steering bar), board (SQLite kanban with atomic CAS claiming), notes, CRM, scheduler, and calendar. Mobile: native iOS app (id6760410435) + PWA. SSE backbone — all clients see changes within ~2s. Comparison table vs DIY tmux / Claude Code alone / Devin (7 capabilities). FAQPage JSON-LD (5 Qs). Updated July 2026.
- [AI Agent Coordination — amux REST API & Atomic Task Claiming (2026)](https://amux.io/features/agent-coordination/): Every amux session gets $AMUX_URL and $AMUX_SESSION at startup. Coordination primitives: atomic SQLite CAS board claim (POST /api/board/:id/claim — 200 if won, 409 if taken), inter-session messaging (POST /api/sessions/:name/send), peer output reading (GET /api/sessions/:name/peek), global memory, and agent discovery (GET /api/sessions). Common patterns: producer-consumer, pipeline, role-based routing. Comparison table vs LangGraph/file-based/Redis (5 approaches). FAQPage JSON-LD (5 Qs). Updated July 2026.
- [Mobile PWA & iOS App — Manage AI Agents from Your Phone (2026)](https://amux.io/features/mobile-pwa/): Native iOS app (App Store id6760410435) + installable PWA for Android. Full dashboard on 375px screen: fleet scan, peek panel, plan strip, subagent switcher, load earlier output, steering bar, board, notes, CRM, scheduler. Touch targets ≥44×44px, safe-area-inset-* for iOS notch, responsive peek reflows to phone width. Offline queue via Background Sync. Remote access: Tailscale (recommended) or amux tunnel (cloud). Comparison table: iOS app vs PWA vs SSH+tmux vs Devin mobile. FAQPage JSON-LD (5 Qs). Updated July 2026.
- [Rust Workspace Architecture — How amux is Built (2026)](https://amux.io/features/single-file-architecture/): amux is a 4-crate Cargo workspace (amux-server, amux-dashboard, amux-core, amux-cli) that compiles to a single binary. The dashboard is real static files (app.js, app.css, index.html, sw.js) in amux-dashboard/static/ — no inline HTML. A background build watcher rebuilds on every commit; the running server self-adopts (exits cleanly, launchd restarts) without manual intervention. No Docker, no config files, no external service dependencies beyond tmux. MIT licensed. Deployment: one binary install via install.sh. Contributing: clone the workspace, cargo check, commit — the auto-builder ships it.
- [amux Tunnel — Expose localhost to the internet](https://amux.io/features/tunnel/): amux tunnel is a built-in HTTP/HTTPS relay that gives your local amux dashboard a stable public URL at https://<id>.t.amux.io/. Machine dials out to the amux cloud gateway — no port forwarding, no firewall changes, no router configuration needed. URL is stable across restarts (derived from token via sha256[:16]). Use cases: mobile dashboard access, webhook testing, OAuth redirect URIs, team demo sharing, CI/CD integration. Limitations: HTTP only, no WebSocket/SSE/TCP, no custom domains, no free tier (requires amux Cloud $20/mo). 7-row comparison table vs ngrok/Cloudflare Tunnel/localtunnel/SSH reverse tunnel/self-host gateway. Self-hosting instructions in cloud/gateway/ (Terraform + GCP). Security: add dashboard password to protect the public URL. BreadcrumbList + Article + FAQPage JSON-LD (7 Qs). Added July 2026.
- [amux Cloud — Tunnel relay for local AI agents](https://amux.io/cloud/): amux Cloud adds exactly one feature beyond the free open-source version: the tunnel relay that gives your local dashboard a stable public HTTPS URL. Everything else (dashboard, agent orchestration, kanban, CRM, email, browser automation, scheduler, mobile PWA, self-healing, MCP) is free MIT-licensed open source. Pricing: $20/month or $200/year. Full OSS vs Cloud feature matrix (14 rows). Self-hosting: tunnel gateway open source in cloud/gateway/ with Terraform + setup script (typically $5-10/mo VM cost). amux Cloud is NOT a cloud AI execution environment — agents run locally, no data on amux servers. FAQ comparing to Devin/Codex/Jules (cloud AI ≠ amux Cloud). BreadcrumbList + WebPage + FAQPage JSON-LD (6 Qs). Added July 2026.

## Comparisons

- [amux vs Hermes Agent](https://amux.io/compare/amux-vs-hermes-agent/): NousResearch's open-source self-improving personal AI daemon (175k GitHub stars, Feb 2026) vs amux parallel coding fleet. Hermes = single persistent agent with cross-session memory, skill self-improvement, 16+ messaging platform connectors, any LLM including local. amux = 10-50 parallel coding agents (Claude Code/Codex/Gemini CLI), shared kanban with atomic claiming, self-healing overnight operation, mobile fleet management. Different jobs: depth for one agent vs throughput for many. FAQPage JSON-LD (5 Qs). July 2026.
- [amux vs Cowork](https://amux.io/compare/amux-vs-cowork/): Claude Cowork (Anthropic's single computer-use agent, available on paid Claude plans) vs amux (parallel coding fleet, open source). Cowork = one agent, GUI/computer-use tasks, desktop app, Claude only. amux = unlimited parallel sessions, coding-agent specific (Claude Code/Codex/Gemini CLI), self-healing watchdog, mobile management, free + API tokens. Throughput comparison: 20 tasks in 1hr (10 parallel amux sessions) vs 10hr (Cowork sequential). FAQPage JSON-LD (5 Qs). July 2026.
- [amux vs OpenClaw](https://amux.io/compare/amux-vs-openclaw/): OpenClaw (formerly Warelay/Moltbot, 347k GitHub stars — most starred repo in history, MIT, OpenAI-backed) vs amux. OpenClaw = messaging-native personal assistant (WhatsApp/Telegram/Slack/Discord/iMessage/20+ more), 100+ AgentSkills, low technical floor, single agent. amux = developer fleet dashboard (web PWA + iOS app), parallel coding agents, kanban coordination, git-safe worktrees, overnight self-healing. Complementary tools for different audiences. FAQPage JSON-LD (5 Qs). July 2026.
- [amux vs Claude Managed Agents](https://amux.io/compare/amux-vs-claude-managed-agents/): Self-hosted alternative to Anthropic's April 2026 Managed Agents launch. $0 session fees vs $0.08/session-hour, model-agnostic, MIT-licensed.
- [amux vs Claude Code Agent Teams — parallel fleet vs sub-task fan-out (2026)](https://amux.io/compare/amux-vs-claude-code-agent-teams/): Accurate comparison of amux and Anthropic's experimental Claude Code Agent Teams (requires CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1, Claude Code v2.1.32+). Agent Teams = parent session spawns sub-agents with git worktree isolation, great for tightly-coupled sub-task fan-out. amux = independent long-running fleet sessions with self-healing, web dashboard, mobile PWA, shared kanban, CRM/email/browser, multi-runtime (Claude Code + Codex + Gemini CLI). 17-row comparison table. "Why not both?" section explains how the two compose. BreadcrumbList + Article + FAQPage JSON-LD (5 Qs). Updated July 2026.
- [amux vs Cursor](https://amux.io/compare/amux-vs-cursor/)
- [amux vs Aider](https://amux.io/compare/amux-vs-aider/): Aider (open-source AI pair programmer, ~25k stars, Apache 2.0, multi-LLM) vs amux. Aider = single-session interactive pair programming with excellent diff quality, 20+ LLM providers. amux = parallel fleet for unattended overnight runs, Claude Code-native, web dashboard, self-healing watchdog. Complementary: Aider for surgical interactive edits, amux for batch fleet runs. FAQPage JSON-LD (5 Qs). July 2026.
- [amux vs GitHub Copilot 2026](https://amux.io/compare/amux-vs-github-copilot/): GitHub Copilot (~1.8M paid users, $10–39/mo, GPT-4o/4.5, IDE-integrated) vs amux (parallel autonomous coding fleet, open source, free + API tokens). Replit Agent excels at zero-setup cloud projects with built-in hosting. amux wins when you have an existing codebase that cannot go to the cloud, need to run dozens of agents in parallel, want model choice (Claude Code + Codex + Gemini CLI), or need mobile monitoring via iOS app. Full 12-row comparison table, "What's New August 2026" section (board analytics, permission audit trail, Connectors, Gmail 4x), 6-question FAQ. Amazon Q excels at AWS-ecosystem integration (CloudFormation, Lambda, IAM) and out-of-box enterprise compliance. amux wins when you need parallel fleet execution (dozens of agents simultaneously), model flexibility (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI — not just Amazon's model), full data residency (code never leaves your machine), or want to avoid per-seat subscription costs ($19/user/month). 12-row comparison table, "Claude Code vs Amazon Q" section, 6-question FAQ. New August 2026.

- [Best AI Agent Orchestrators 2026](https://amux.io/lists/best-ai-agent-orchestrators-2026/): amux, LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, OpenAI Symphony, Claude Managed Agents, Hermes Agent, dmux, OpenHands, sandboxed.sh — architecture, OSS status, when to use.
- [Best Open Source AI Coding Tools 2026](https://amux.io/lists/open-source-ai-coding-tools-2026/): OSS-only — amux, Aider, Cline/Roo Code, OpenHands, Continue.dev, Goose, Antigravity CLI. License, language, model provider.
- [Best AI Tools for Solopreneurs 2026](https://amux.io/lists/ai-tools-for-solopreneurs-2026/): 10 tools — what each replaces, monthly cost, time saved. amux, Claude, Cursor, Notion AI, Copilot, Perplexity, Make, v0, Bolt.new, Linear AI.
- [AI Agent Frameworks Compared 2026](https://amux.io/lists/ai-agent-frameworks-comparison-2026/): amux, LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, Semantic Kernel, Bee Agent, Agency Swarm, MetaGPT — language, multi-agent, state management, best use cases.

- [Declarative AI Agent Setup](https://amux.io/guides/declarative-ai-agent-setup/): Configure your entire AI engineering team with a single YAML file (a "vertical") using amux IaC. Covers declarative vs imperative setup, idempotent apply, GitOps workflow, multi-runtime teams (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI), skins/personas, version control, and CI/CD integration. New August 2026.

- [Agent Multiplexer — Glossary](https://amux.io/glossary/agent-multiplexer/): Full definition of "agent multiplexer" — a platform that runs, monitors, and self-heals dozens of parallel AI coding agents from one dashboard. Covers how it works (tmux sessions + watchdog + REST API), comparison table (raw tmux vs shell scripts vs agent multiplexer across 8 capabilities), 6-question FAQ (FAQPage JSON-LD), Article + DefinedTerm + BreadcrumbList JSON-LD. Distinguishes multiplexers from task queues: task queues are stateless; agent multiplexers are stateful (sessions hold context across tasks). amux is the open-source reference implementation. Updated August 2026 with comparison table, FAQ, and EXP-051 CTA.
- [AI Agent Fleet — Glossary](https://amux.io/glossary/ai-agent-fleet/): Full definition of "AI agent fleet" — a coordinated group of AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI) running concurrently under a shared orchestration layer. Covers fleet components (agent sessions/tmux, task queue/kanban, self-healing watchdog, SSE monitoring dashboard), fleet vs single-agent vs orchestrator vs task queue comparison table (5-row), fleet sizing (200-400 MB per agent), multi-runtime fleets, and how amux manages fleets (session cloning, age-weighted pickup, GitHub App token shim, SSE health signal). DefinedTerm + Article + BreadcrumbList + FAQPage JSON-LD (6 Qs). EXP-065 CTA. New August 2026.
- [AI Agent Control Plane — Glossary](https://amux.io/glossary/ai-agent-control-plane/): Full definition of "AI agent control plane" — the infrastructure layer that manages lifecycle, health, task routing, credential scoping, and self-healing for a fleet of AI coding agents. Distinguishes control planes from orchestrators (orchestrators sequence workflows; control planes manage the infrastructure of agents themselves) and task queues (stateless vs stateful). Covers the 6 things a control plane manages: session lifecycle, health/self-healing, task routing (kanban board), credential scoping (OAuth broker), observability (dashboard + iOS app + REST API), and scheduling. 3-column comparison table (task queue vs orchestrator vs control plane), 6-question FAQ (FAQPage JSON-LD), DefinedTerm + Article + BreadcrumbList JSON-LD. amux is the open-source reference implementation. New August 2026 with EXP-052 CTA.
- [Reverse Tunnel — Glossary](https://amux.io/glossary/reverse-tunnel/): Definition of "reverse tunnel" — a technique where a machine inside a private network dials outbound to a public relay, letting the relay forward inbound traffic back without opening firewall ports. Covers how it works step-by-step, reverse tunnel vs port forwarding comparison, open-source options (ngrok vs localtunnel vs Cloudflare Tunnel vs amux tunnel) with honest trade-off table, security considerations, and 6-question FAQ (FAQPage JSON-LD). DefinedTerm + Article + BreadcrumbList JSON-LD. amux tunnel is the built-in option (stable token-derived URL, no extra install, gated on amux cloud). New August 2026.
